output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the failure of the east-side chiller (CH-2), which left floors 6-8 hot from 4 to 19 August. Room comfort on those floors fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores were 6.8 for checkouts on 5-20 August, then recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 were flat overall. Cleanliness, check-in and kiosk scores did not move, and inspection pass rates held at 95-96%. Queue times were also steady. The evidence doesn't support blaming Orrin or the kiosks, so don't serve notice and don't pull the kiosks. The rate increase may have contributed slightly to a small value-score dip on floors 1-5, but that dip is within the normal August pattern, so I can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate on this evidence. Don't drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score, because that hides a real failure. Next steps: reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spares, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Keep watching the rate effect. I'm fairly confident, and I did not collect any extra evidence because none was likely to change these actions.
